concepts.name: Data centres and servers
concepts.summary: Recall that cloud services run on providers' physical servers, storage and networks housed in large data centres.

concepts.name: Cloud computing definition
concepts.summary: Recall that cloud computing delivers shared computing resources over a network on demand, rented rather than owned.

concepts.name: Essential cloud characteristics
concepts.summary: Explain on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity and measured service.

concepts.name: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS models
concepts.summary: Distinguish infrastructure, platform and software as a service by what the provider supplies and what the customer manages.

concepts.name: Deployment models
concepts.summary: Describe public, private, hybrid and multi-cloud deployments and who owns and uses each.

concepts.name: Pay-as-you-go pricing
concepts.summary: Explain that customers pay for metered usage instead of buying hardware upfront, shifting capital expense to operating expense.

misconceptions.text: The cloud is a mysterious place with no physical hardware behind it.
Cloud computing is just storing files online.
Cloud is always cheaper than running your own servers.

concepts.name: Virtualization and hypervisors
concepts.summary: Explain how a hypervisor shares one physical host among isolated virtual machines, and tell type 1 from type 2.

concepts.name: Regions and availability zones
concepts.summary: Choose regions and zones for a simple workload, knowing a region contains multiple isolated zones.

concepts.name: Shared responsibility model
aliases: security of vs in the cloud
concepts.summary: Apply the split of security duties between provider and customer for IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.

concepts.name: Elasticity versus scalability
concepts.summary: Distinguish scalability as capacity to grow from elasticity as automatic matching of capacity to demand, and apply vertical and horizontal scaling.

concepts.name: Matching service model to need
concepts.summary: Pick IaaS, PaaS or SaaS for a simple scenario based on required control and management effort.

concepts.name: Resource pooling and multi-tenancy
concepts.summary: Explain how many customers share pooled hardware while logically isolated from each other.

misconceptions.text: The provider is responsible for securing everything you put in the cloud.
Elasticity and scalability mean the same thing.
A virtual machine is a separate physical computer.

concepts.name: Cloud cost analysis
concepts.summary: Compare cloud and on-premises total cost of ownership, including usage patterns, data transfer and idle resources.

concepts.name: Pricing options trade-offs
concepts.summary: Analyse when on-demand, reserved or committed, and interruptible spot capacity fit different workloads.

concepts.name: Hybrid and multi-cloud rationale
concepts.summary: Analyse the drivers and costs of hybrid and multi-cloud, such as compliance, latency, resilience and added complexity.

concepts.name: Auto scaling policies
concepts.summary: Configure scaling rules and load balancing that add or remove instances based on metrics.

concepts.name: High availability across zones
concepts.summary: Design a workload that survives a zone failure by distributing redundant components across availability zones.

concepts.name: Data residency and compliance
concepts.summary: Analyse how regulations and data location constrain region choice and service use.

concepts.name: Responsibility boundaries by service
concepts.summary: Analyse who owns patching, identity, data and configuration for a given service and find gaps.

misconceptions.text: Running in the cloud automatically makes an application highly available.
Multi-cloud always improves resilience and lowers cost.
Autoscaling removes the need for capacity planning or cost monitoring.

concepts.name: Workload placement evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate which workloads belong in public, private, hybrid or on-premises environments against technical and business criteria.

concepts.name: Migration strategy selection
concepts.summary: Judge between rehost, replatform, refactor, replace and retire for an application, weighing effort against benefit.

concepts.name: Resilience and disaster recovery
concepts.summary: Analyse recovery objectives and compare backup, pilot light, warm standby and active-active strategies across regions.

concepts.name: Vendor lock-in assessment
concepts.summary: Evaluate lock-in risk from proprietary services against portability costs and the benefits of managed services.

concepts.name: Cloud financial governance
concepts.summary: Assess cost controls such as tagging, budgets, showback and rightsizing for their effect on spending accountability.

concepts.name: Performance and latency trade-offs
concepts.summary: Analyse how region distance, data gravity and egress charges shape architecture and performance.

concepts.name: Provider and service evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate providers and services by SLAs, compliance attestations, support and service fit.

misconceptions.text: Lifting and shifting an application to the cloud delivers cloud benefits unchanged.
A provider's SLA guarantees your application will never go down.
Avoiding lock-in is always worth the cost of using only generic services.

concepts.name: Cloud strategy design
concepts.summary: Create an organisation-wide cloud strategy aligning deployment models, service models, governance and business goals.

concepts.name: Multi-region resilient architecture
concepts.summary: Design architectures spanning regions that meet stated availability, latency, consistency and cost targets.

concepts.name: Landing zone and governance framework
concepts.summary: Create a multi-account governance framework with guardrails, identity boundaries and standard controls.

concepts.name: Cloud risk and compliance critique
concepts.summary: Evaluate risks such as provider concentration, misconfiguration and jurisdictional exposure, and justify mitigations.

concepts.name: Economic modelling of cloud
concepts.summary: Critique and build business cases and unit-cost models that test when cloud, repatriation or hybrid is justified.

concepts.name: Sustainability in cloud design
concepts.summary: Evaluate energy efficiency and carbon impact of placement, utilisation and architecture choices.

concepts.name: Cloud portfolio evolution
concepts.summary: Create a roadmap and exit strategy that adapt the cloud portfolio as services, costs and regulations change.

misconceptions.text: A single cloud strategy with one standard architecture fits every workload in an organisation.
Moving to the cloud transfers accountability for compliance and risk to the provider.
Cloud is inherently greener, so sustainability needs no design attention.
